📚 1. 15 Từ Vựng Cốt Lõi (Kèm Phát Âm Audio Bản Xứ)

Bấm vào nút 🔊 để nghe phát âm chuẩn bản xứ của từng từ vựng (trên iPhone, hãy gạt cần rung sang chế độ Chuông để bật loa ngoài). Hệ thống tối ưu hiển thị linh hoạt trên cả điện thoại, máy tính bảng và máy tính:

⚠️ BẠN ĐANG MỞ Ở CHẾ ĐỘ XEM TRƯỚC — ÂM THANH SẼ KHÔNG CHẠY
Ứng dụng Tệp (Files) và Zalo trên iPhone chặn JavaScript, nên nút 🔊, chấm điểm và micro đều bị vô hiệu.
👉 Hãy mở bài học bằng đường link https:// mà giáo viên gửi (bấm vào link trong Zalo ➔ chọn biểu tượng la bàn Safari).
Bấm để máy tự động đọc lần lượt từng từ và hiển thị theo dõi (phù hợp học trên điện thoại)
1. cosmos (n)
/ˈkɒzmɒs/
vũ trụ bao la (= the universe — thường dùng với mạo từ 'the cosmos')
Collocation: explore the cosmos, mysteries of the cosmos
"For centuries, astronomers have built powerful telescopes to unlock the mysteries of the cosmos."
2. satellite (n)
/ˈsætəlaɪt/
vệ tinh (nhân tạo hoặc tự nhiên quay quanh hành tinh)
Collocation: weather satellite, communications satellite, launch a satellite
"Modern weather satellites enable meteorologists to track typhoons and warn coastal communities early."
3. orbit (n/v)
/ˈɔːbɪt/
quỹ đạo; bay quanh quỹ đạo của một hành tinh/ngôi sao
Collocation: in orbit around the Earth, orbit the sun, low Earth orbit
"Thousands of commercial satellites currently orbit the Earth to provide global internet coverage."
4. astronaut (n)
/ˈæstrənɔːt/
phi hành gia, nhà du hành vũ trụ
Collocation: train astronauts, crew of astronauts, aboard the space station
"Living in zero gravity for months weakens the bones and muscles of astronauts."
5. colonize (v)
/ˈkɒlənaɪz/
định cư, lập thuộc địa/khu định cư của con người trên hành tinh khác (n: colonization)
Collocation: colonize Mars, space colonization, colonize another planet
"Some visionary billionaires believe humanity will colonize Mars before the end of this century."
6. lunar (adj)
/ˈluːnə(r)/
thuộc về Mặt Trăng (lunar module / lunar surface / lunar base)
Collocation: lunar surface, permanent lunar base, lunar exploration
"Space agencies plan to build a permanent research station on the lunar south pole by 2035."
7. celestial (adj)
/səˈlestiəl/
thuộc về bầu trời, thiên thể trong vũ trụ (celestial bodies = các thiên thể: sao, hành tinh, thiên thạch)
Collocation: celestial bodies, distant celestial objects
"Mining asteroids and other celestial bodies could provide rare minerals for clean energy technology."
8. gravity (n)
/ˈɡrævəti/
trọng lực, lực hấp dẫn
Collocation: zero gravity, Earth's gravity, force of gravity
"Conducting medical experiments in zero gravity allows scientists to develop new pharmaceutical treatments."
9. propulsion (n)
/prəˈpʌlʃn/
hệ thống đẩy, lực đẩy (tên lửa, tàu vũ trụ — v: propel)
Collocation: rocket propulsion, nuclear propulsion system
"Breakthroughs in rocket propulsion have dramatically reduced the cost of launching cargo into space."
10. debris (n)
/ˈdebriː/
mảnh vỡ, rác thải vũ trụ (space debris — âm 's' cuối câm, danh từ không đếm được)
Collocation: space debris, orbital debris, clear dangerous debris
"Millions of pieces of floating space debris pose a grave collision threat to active satellites."
11. pioneer (v/n)
/ˌpaɪəˈnɪə(r)/
tiên phong mở đường; người/quốc gia tiên phong (adj: pioneering — mang tính tiên phong)
Collocation: pioneer new technology, pioneering research
"Space agencies have pioneered water filtration and solar technologies that now benefit millions on Earth."
12. astronomical (adj)
/ˌæstrəˈnɒmɪkl/
(1) thuộc thiên văn học; (2) (chi phí/con số) khổng lồ, cao ngất ngưởng
Collocation: astronomical cost, astronomical sum of money
"Critics argue that launching manned missions to Mars requires an astronomical amount of taxpayer money."
13. feasible (adj)
/ˈfiːzəbl/
khả thi, có thể thực hiện được về mặt kỹ thuật và kinh tế (n: feasibility)
Collocation: economically feasible, technically feasible, a feasible solution
"Reusable rockets have made commercial space travel far more economically feasible."
14. frontiers (n)
/ˈfrʌntɪəz/
những biên giới mới, những chân trời khám phá mới của khoa học
Collocation: push the frontiers of science, new frontiers of knowledge
"Exploring deep space pushes the frontiers of human knowledge and inspires young engineers."
15. imperative (adj/n)
/ɪmˈperətɪv/
cấp bách, bắt buộc phải làm ngay (= vital / crucial — dùng trong cấu trúc giả định C1: It is imperative that...)
Collocation: It is imperative that..., moral imperative
"It is imperative that governments solve urgent problems on Earth while investing wisely in science."

⚙️ 2. Bài Giảng Ngữ Pháp 2 Tầng (Grammar Masterclass)

🟢 Tầng 1: Tương Lai Hoàn Thành (Future Perfect: will have + V3/ed) & Động Từ Khuyết Thiếu Suy Luận Quá Khứ (Modal Perfect)

• 1. Thì Tương lai Hoàn thành (S + will have + V3/ed): Diễn tả một hành động sẽ hoàn tất trước một mốc thời gian trong tương lai (luôn đi kèm By + năm tương lai: By 2040, By the end of this century).
  Ví dụ: By 2040, international space agencies will have established a permanent research base on the lunar surface.

• 2. Thì Tương lai Tiếp diễn (S + will be + V-ing): Diễn tả hành động sẽ đang diễn ra tại một thời điểm tương lai.
  Ví dụ: In thirty years' time, private companies will be mining rare minerals from asteroids.

• 3. Động từ Khuyết thiếu Suy luận trong Quá khứ (must / might / could / cannot + have + V3/ed):
  - must have + V3/ed: Chắc chắn đã xảy ra (dựa trên bằng chứng).
  - might / could have + V3/ed: Có lẽ đã xảy ra trong quá khứ.
  Ví dụ: Ancient riverbeds on Mars prove that liquid water must have existed on the planet billions of years ago.

🔵 Tầng 2: Thức Giả Định Hiện Tại (Present Subjunctive) — Cấu Trúc Kiến Nghị C1-C2 Đắt Giá Nhất

• Công thức chuẩn học thuật khi viết câu Kết luận hoặc Giải pháp trong Writing Task 2:
  It is imperative / essential / vital / crucial that + S + (should) + V (nguyên mẫu không chia s/es/ed)
  Ví dụ 1 (Chủ động): It is imperative that every spacefaring nation reduce (không thêm -s!) orbital debris.
  Ví dụ 2 (Bị động): It is vital that public funds be allocated (dùng 'be', không dùng 'are'!) to both poverty reduction and scientific research.

🎯 20 Câu Test Từ Vựng (Vocabulary Mastery Test)

1. The James Webb Space Telescope allows astronomers to peer deeper into the ________ than ever before.
2. Meteorological ________ orbiting the Earth help scientists monitor global warming and hurricane paths.
3. The International Space Station completes sixteen full ________ around the Earth every single day.
4. Every ________ aboard the spacecraft must exercise for two hours daily to prevent bone loss.
5. Before humans can ________ Mars, engineers must figure out how to produce oxygen and water on the red planet.
6. In 1969, Apollo 11 astronauts collected rock samples from the ________ surface and brought them back to Earth.
7. Telescopes protect our planet by tracking asteroids, comets, and other ________ bodies near Earth.
8. Without the pull of Earth's ________, water droplets float freely inside the cabin of a space station.
9. Engineers are testing nuclear thermal ________ systems that could cut travel time to Mars in half.
10. Old broken satellites and rocket stages create dangerous clouds of space ________ in low Earth orbit.
11. NASA scientists ________ many inventions, such as memory foam and scratch-resistant lenses, that we use daily.
12. Building a self-sustaining city on another planet would require an ________ amount of financial investment.
13. Thanks to reusable boosters, launching commercial communication satellites has become much more ________.
14. Scientific curiosity drives humanity to push the ________ of physics, medicine, and deep-ocean exploration.
15. With climate change accelerating, it is ________ that nations transition to clean renewable energy immediately.
16. [Ôn tập Unit 25] Volunteering to help flood victims without expecting any reward is an act of pure ________.
17. [Ôn tập Unit 24] Chronic sleep deprivation can severely ________ an astronaut's reaction time and judgement.
18. [Ôn tập Unit 23] Before publishing a scientific claim, editors must ________ the experimental data.
19. [Ôn tập Unit 22] Critics argue that governments should ________ more tax revenue to hospitals rather than space rockets.
20. [Ôn tập Unit 17] Solar panels on the space station absorb sunlight and ________ it into electricity.
Điểm: 0/20

⚙️ 10 Câu Test Ngữ Pháp Ứng Dụng (Grammar Mastery Test)

1. Future Perfect Tense: By the year 2045, engineers ________ a permanent research base on the lunar surface.
2. Modal Perfect of Deduction: Dried-up river valleys on Mars prove that liquid water ________ on the planet in the past.
3. Present Subjunctive (C1): It is imperative that every space agency ________ strict rules to reduce orbital debris.
4. Passive Subjunctive (C1): It is vital that taxpayer money ________ wisely between terrestrial needs and space research.
5. Note that 'debris' is uncountable: Millions of pieces of space debris ________ currently orbiting the Earth at high speed.
6. Future Continuous: This time next decade, private aerospace companies ________ tourists into low Earth orbit.
7. Scientists discovered organic molecules on the meteorite, which suggests that microbial life ________ there long ago.
8. Not only ________ satellite technology improve weather forecasting, but it also enables global navigation.
9. ________ the astronomical cost of space missions, they have pioneered countless medical inventions.
10. What ________ young people to study astrophysics is humanity's innate curiosity about the cosmos.
Điểm: 0/10

📰 IELTS Academic Reading: Passage & Questions

[Paragraph A - The Argument Against Astronomical Space Expenditure]
Whenever governments announce multi-billion-dollar missions to build a lunar base or send astronauts to Mars, fierce public debate erupts. Critics argue that spending astronomical sums of taxpayer money on exploring the cosmos is unjustifiable when millions of citizens on Earth still suffer from poverty, famine, and inadequate healthcare. Furthermore, rocket launches consume vast resources and leave clouds of dangerous debris in low Earth orbit. From this viewpoint, it is imperative that humanity solve terrestrial crises before attempting to colonize distant planets.

[Paragraph B - Everyday Technologies Pioneered by Space Research]
Despite these criticisms, scientists maintain that space exploration delivers immense practical benefits to people on Earth. Over the past half-century, aerospace research has pioneered hundreds of life-saving technologies, including water purification filters, portable medical scanners, and high-efficiency solar panels. Today, a global network of satellites in orbit monitors climate change, predicts catastrophic typhoons, and enables rural telemedicine. In addition, medical experiments conducted in zero gravity aboard space stations help researchers develop new treatments for bone loss andchronic diseases.

[Paragraph C - Future Frontiers and Sustainable Space Exploration]
Looking ahead, advancements in reusable rocket propulsion have made space missions far more economically feasible. By the end of this century, scientists project that humanity will have established permanent scientific outposts on the Moon and begun extracting rare minerals from celestial asteroids. Provided that spacefaring nations cooperate to clear orbital debris and maintain a balanced budget, pushing the frontiers of space science will secure humanity's long-term survival.
Điểm: 0/6
